ownership_reason: Only the gold holds the directory of the requiring file together with the individual segments of the path; the extension stripping, the relative/top-level decision, the './' placement and the pass-through hand the two strings along. The trigger's target 'baz' lies outside the requiring file's directory 'foo/', so no path without '..' leads to it from that file: an edit above the gold can only make the result right by handing the gold another requiring file or by computing the resolution itself (a second implementation outside the gold, e.g. java.net.URI resolution or PathUtil.collapseDots), and reading '$' in the gold's output as a separator drops the 'module$' part of names that climb past the top directory. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc promises relative addressing with ./ and ../ based on the current filename; PathUtil.collapseDots (reached through PathUtil.makeAbsolute from DepsGenerator) removes the previous fragment for every '..' fragment ('a/b/../c' results in 'a/c'); toModuleName(String) and its passing tests pin the conversion that the gold hands the resolved path to. The gold's javadoc promises the module name of the file that the path leads to from the directory of the requiring file: '../baz' from 'foo/bar' leads to 'baz', whose module name is 'module$baz'.
